name: wedding_fund_balance_forecast
description: Shows the wedding fund balance on each payment due date, counting monthly savings and the family contribution, and says how much is missing if the fund falls short.
formula: Go through the payments in order of due date. Balance before a payment = current_savings + monthly_saving x (number of saving dates after today and on or before that due date) + contribution_amount (only if contribution_date is on or before that due date) - the amounts of all earlier payments. Saving dates are the same day of the month as today, one month after another (if a month is too short, use its last day). Balance after payment = balance before - amount due. Shortfall = the amount by which the balance after payment is below zero, or 0 if it is not. The running balance carries on to the next payment even when it is negative. Payments due on the same date are taken in the order given.

inputs.name: current_savings
inputs.description: Money already saved for the wedding today, in your currency.

inputs.name: monthly_saving
inputs.description: Amount you add to the wedding fund each month, in your currency. Use the result of the monthly surplus step. It can be zero or negative.

inputs.name: today
inputs.description: Today's date. Savings are counted from the day after today.

inputs.name: payments
inputs.description: The wedding payments, one item for each. Each item has name (text, for example payment 1), amount (money in your currency) and due_date (a date). Use the results of the payment schedule step.

inputs.name: contribution_amount
inputs.description: Money you expect from family and partner's family, in your currency, paid into the wedding fund in one go. Use 0 if none is expected.

inputs.name: contribution_date
inputs.description: The date the contribution is expected. Ignored if the contribution amount is 0.

output.description: One item for each payment, in order of due date. Each item has: name (text), due_date (a date), amount_due, balance_before_payment (fund balance on that date before paying), balance_after_payment (balance after paying; may be negative), and shortfall (amount missing after paying, or 0 if the fund covers it). Amounts are money in your currency.
